But the direct-path proxy may just be reflecting real bigram statistics rather than an artifact: doubled letters are genuinely rare in English/romaji/python, so a negative B[c,c] across the board is plausible rather than a quirk of embedding geometry. What's odd is that space (index 26) is only mildly negative compared to letters, even though space-space transitions should be essentially nonexistent in real text, which makes me question whether this direct-path term is really capturing bigram log-probs or something else entirely.

To test this, I want to check vowel/consonant block structure — consonant-to-vowel transitions should be relatively positive and consonant-to-consonant relatively negative (especially for romaji), so I'm computing block averages for vowel-vowel, vowel-consonant, consonant-vowel, and consonant-consonant pairs, along with the space row/column to see word-boundary effects.

from sklearn.decomposition import FastICA
from scipy.stats import kurtosis
w0=W['ln1_w.0']; w2=W['ln2_w.0']

def OV(l,j):

T,_=rs(np.vstack([W['W_v.0'][64:128]*w0, W['W_v.0'][320:384]*w0]),40)

Tp=T-P@(P.T@T); U,s,_=np.linalg.svd(Tp,full_matrices=False); Tp=U[:,:28]
alive=np.linalg.norm(W['W_fc.0'],axis=1)>1
F=(W['W_fc.0']*w2)[alive]

ica=FastICA(n_components=28,random_state=0,max_iter=10000,whiten='unit-variance',fun='logcosh',tol=1e-5)

kc=kurtosis(G@E.T,axis=0); order=np.argsort(-kc); E=E[order]

D=Temb@Tp.T
vow=[12,13,16,21,25]; cons=[c for c in range(26) if c not in vow]; sp=26
def blocks(B,name):
    B=B-B.mean(1,keepdims=True)
    def m(r,c):
        vals=[B[i,j] for i in r for j in c if i!=j]; return np.mean(vals)
    print(f'{name}: VV {m(vow,vow):+.3f} VC {m(vow,cons):+.3f} CV {m(cons,vow):+.3f} CC {m(cons,cons):+.3f} | diag mean {np.mean(np.diag(B)[:27]):+.3f} | sp->sp {B[sp,sp]:+.3f} V->sp {m(vow,[sp]):+.3f} C->sp {m(cons,[sp]):+.3f} sp->V {m([sp],vow):+.3f} sp->C {m([sp],cons):+.3f}')
for heads in [[(3,5)],[(3,1)],[(3,5),(3,1)],[(2,1)],[(3,0)]]:
    Ou=sum([(OV(l,j)@D.T).T/np.linalg.norm((OV(l,j)@D.T).T,axis=1,keepdims=True) for (l,j) in heads])
    Ou=Ou-Ou[:27].mean(0)
    B=D[:27]@Ou[:27].T
    blocks(B,str(heads)+' direct(t_cur . o_next)')
    # prev-token path: OV0(5) t_prev . o_next  (skip-trigram-ish from previous token)
    B2=(OV(0,5)@D[:27].T).T@Ou[:27].T
    blocks(B2,str(heads)+' viaL0H5')
